changes.title: Town editor!
changes.text: New Towns tab: every town of the save, with filters by player, faction and name, and a summary of the town hall, fort, mage guild, dwellings, Grail, garrison and heroes in town. The town window changes the buildings (laid out as in the game's town hall; what a building needs is built by itself, and the editor asks when other buildings change), the garrison and the mage guild spells, by level and school as in the hero's spell book. Neutral towns are not edited. The changes show up in the Changed block.

changes.title: Presets!
changes.text: As in version 2.05, only for every editor: the hero window, the town window and the Resources tab got the “Save preset…” and “Load preset…” buttons. A preset is kept in the browser under its own name; checkboxes pick what to save and what to load: each hero attribute on its own and the other tabs as a whole (the backpack and the spells can be added or replaced), a town's buildings, garrison and mage guild, each resource. The hint of a checkbox shows what will be saved or what loading changes. What the save's edition lacks is skipped; a town of another faction gets only the buildings every town has. Loading changes only the window; the save gets the changes after “Apply”.
The Heroes, Resources and Towns tabs stay inactive until a save is open: a hint says what to do first.
On the first visit the interface language follows the browser. A language you pick yourself is still remembered.

changes.title: Equipment editor!
changes.text: New Equipment tab in the hero window, with the slots laid out as on the game's hero screen. Put on and take off any artifact that fits, switch war machines and the spell book on and off. A combination artifact takes its slots by itself. A checkbox decides what happens to what comes off: unticked, it is deleted; ticked, it goes to the backpack, and the editor asks if there is not enough room. The changes show up in the Changed block.
Armageddon's Blade campaign saves from Complete: backpack artifacts no longer slide one slot over (and no longer land in the fifth misc slot), and the player treasury is found right away.
Restoration of Erathia campaign saves from Complete are recognised as The Restoration of Erathia, not The Shadow of Death.

summary: 20 years later - off to the web! Step one: dragging everything we had into the new world.

changes.title: Heroes 3 SaveEditor Web version.
changes.text: A new life for Heroes III SaveEditor 2.05 (hmm3se.exe) by the VItonIC Group creative team, author Ztalker. The editor moved from a Windows .exe to the browser. No install, no gzip.exe, nothing to unpack: open a save, edit, save. Your saves never leave your machine.

changes.title: Horn of the Abyss!
changes.text: With the project back to life, the editor now supports the latest popular expansion.
English is now the main language, Russian is still here. Switch it any time.
Dark and light themes, both in the spirit of good old Heroes 3. The default theme is "System".

The interface got a careful rework: more information on screen, groups and elements set apart visually. New filters for quick search. The search itself was revised: it finds more often and often picks the right hero or treasury by itself. Picking artifacts is more interactive. The spell screen was redrawn from scratch: spells are laid out by level and school, and whole groups can be added or removed in one click. The creature, artifact and spell lists offer only what the save's edition has.
The jokes and wisecracks of the old version moved in too.

What the editor does in Horn of the Abyss: it edits heroes of the new towns - Cove, Factory and Bulwark, each with its own badge. Their classes and creatures are in, along with the HotA artifacts and the Interference and Runes skills. The hero search knows 16 HotA campaign heroes. HotA saves older than 1.8 have no Factory, Bulwark or Runes, and the editor does not offer them there. The level cap in HotA is 74.
Just drop a save onto the window.
Ctrl+O opens a file, Ctrl+S saves it.
Saving goes through the system "Save as" window: the default name gets an se_ prefix, the original stays untouched.
A warning about unsaved edits when you close the tab or open another file.
The editor figures out what wrote the save: Armageddon's Blade (GOG version included), The Shadow of Death, Heroes Chronicles, HD Edition or Horn of the Abyss.
HD Edition support is officially on.

The editor tells the edition by the save header, not just by the heroes. When the header leaves no doubt (The Restoration of Erathia, HD Edition, Heroes Chronicles, Armageddon's Blade, Horn of the Abyss), the edition in the header bar cannot be changed; otherwise the list greys out the editions that could not have written the save.
Level and experience are linked: change the level and the experience follows; with "Level follows the experience" checked it is the other way round.
Spells are laid out like a spell book: levels 1-5 down, Air, Fire, Water and Earth across. Magic Arrow and Visions show up in every school with a four-element badge.
Every spell has a purpose badge: damage, buff, protection, weakening, control, healing, battlefield, special, summoning, adventure. The same badges filter the list.
Hover over a spell and a hint tells its school, level and what it does.

Every artifact in the backpack list has a category badge: attack, defense, power, knowledge, combined, luck and morale, skills, magic, immunity, troops, adventure, resources, weakening, special. The same badges filter the list, and a "+" button right in the list puts an artifact into the backpack without closing the list. What the hero already carries is highlighted.
The artifact list shows only what the save's edition knows. The spell book, the spell scroll and the catapult are gone from it altogether: the game glitches with them in the backpack.
Every secondary skill has its own badge, in the list and next to the field. The level shows as stripes: one for basic, two for advanced, three for expert.

In the army every creature has its town's badge, in the list and next to the field, on the town's colour. The list holds only the creatures the save's edition knows; the hero's own town comes first, level 1 to 7.
The found hero shows the town of their class, and each creature in their army shows its town.
Movement points left today and movement per day: both are editable.
When the editor changes the edition by itself, the edition list in the header winks so you can see what changed.
Fixed old bugs nobody noticed in 20 years (well, almost nobody).
Searching for "Adela" no longer finds "Adelaide".
Saves with a broken gzip checksum (and Heroes writes exactly those) open without complaints.
Half-learned spells in a save no longer get lost when a hero is written back.
Movement points are read and written in full (4 bytes), not as one byte like 2.05 did.
Presets are off to the warehouse for now, but they will be back soon.
